answer:
The Spanish verbs note now has a game on its App side, called Verb Rush. I ran the app check, and it came back with only one flag: no control in the app edits the note's text. That's intended, since the game only reads your table. I couldn't play it through on a phone, so give it a quick try.

- **A round:** 10 questions, each a four-choice quiz, and you have 8 seconds per question. You get three lives. A wrong answer or running out of time costs a life.
- **Directions:** some questions go Spanish to English and some English to Spanish, mixed at random.
- **Scoring:** faster answers and combos score more. A new best score or a flawless round sets off confetti.
- **Adaptive:** verbs you miss come back more often, and each verb has a 5-pip mastery meter.
- **Daily habit:** it tracks your day streak, best score and rounds played today. The end screen lists the verbs you missed.
- **Your table:** it reads the Spanish | English table in the note. New rows join the game automatically, and it needs at least 4 rows.
